problems.problem: Prose and exactness: ‘things left in chaos’ renders Guo Xiang’s 渾沌 (undivided, unknowing simplicity; his words are 渾沌無知而任其自復). In plain English at six in the morning, ‘chaos’ means disorder, and it sits just after a passage in which the Vital Principle blames government for the empire’s confusion. So the sentence seems to have Guo Xiang recommend leaving things in disorder, which is the opposite of his point. The key verse’s own translation gives this state as ‘a simple purity’.
problems.fix: Change the reading’s last clause to ‘for things left unknowing to return of themselves never leave their root.’ That follows 渾沌無知而任其自復，乃能終身不離其本也 from the verified evidence. The full sentence becomes: ‘Pressed again, the Vital Principle tells the Spirit of the Clouds to rest in inaction; Guo Xiang, on chapter 11, reads the return as true only when made without knowing, for things left unknowing to return of themselves never leave their root.’ It is 42 words, and entry-check comes back ok (scratch/critic5/f14.json).
